notes:
Snapshot of current state / shorthand from calls and threads:
- Account: Sable Horizon (factory floor autonomy + remote ops). High-value: reduce unplanned downtime via predictive maintenance + lower false positives in visual inspection.
- Ask: Dedicated pool (reserved) with deterministic throughput for on-prem & VPC connectivity; want option for private control plane.
- Sizing: optimistic 8 A100-eq reserved; peak bursting to hosted for 2x concurrency during firmware update windows. SE flagged quantized models for cost.
- Performance targets (customer-stated): p95 latency <200ms for text-only control prompts, end-to-end <400ms for vision+prompt flows; steady-state throughput ~12K tokens/min per model instance; concurrency target 150-200 sessions.
- SLA negotiation highlights: they want 99.99% uptime for dedicated pool across REGION, Redwood standard is 99.95 — legal pushing back. Key asks from Sable Horizon legal: explicit credit schedule, shorter maintenance windows, and guaranteed NOC escalation matrix.
- Proposed credit schedule (initial Redw. offer): 99.95-99.99 = no credit; 99.9-99.95 = 10% monthly credit; 99.0-99.9 = 25% credit; <99.0 => 50% credit + right to terminate. Customer counter: wants narrower buckets and higher credits for any drop below 99.99.
- Maintenance windows: Sable requests maintenance <=4 hours/month, preferably 01:00-05:00 UTC weekend slot for production. Redwood asks for 6 hours quarterly for major OS/kernel updates; compromise needed.
- Support SLOs asked: P1 phone + 15m response (on-call), P2 1h response, P3 4h response. Redwood current enterprise SLOs: P1 30m, P2 2h, P3 8h. Procurement flagged as blocker.
- Security: must support SSO/SAML, customer-managed KMS, audit log retention 7 years (they will push), data residency for EU/NA regional separation for telemetry.
- Contract preferences: 12-24 month committed reserved capacity with ramp schedule. Prefer monthly billing but OK with invoiced quarterly if credits applied.
- Quote feedback: procurement asked to see SLA text with explicit exclusion list (force majeure, scheduled maintenance with >72h notice, customer misconfig). They want definition of "downtime" for multi-tenant fallback.
- POC plan: 2-week capacity validation run on reserved pool + 48h failover test to hosted fallback. Required before final sign-off.
- Next ops item: legal redline meeting scheduled 2026-03-18 (Maya + Liam + Redwood legal) -> produce modified SLA draft by 2026-03-15.
- Quotes/notes pulled from FF transcript: "we can't accept anything less than 99.99 for mission-critical lines" (CTO). "If we lose processing during firmware push windows it costs us >$150k/hour" (Ops lead).
- Jira incidents referenced during tests: RDW-INC-2319: tokenization mismatch on vision pipeline; mitigation: adjust padding policy.
